title: adaptive-queue-fence-epoched-hedge
author: Marisol Vega
description: Summary: Introduce an adaptive queue-fence with epoched hedging to reduce starvation and pathological queue growth under skewed continuous-batching workloads. Motivation: Long-tail latency for small, KV-heavy requests increases when continuous-batcher windows preferentially pack throughput-oriented inputs; persistent lockstep arrivals can starve lighter but latency-sensitive traffic and delay KV cache warmups. This change adds an epoched fence that periodically hedges admission for starved lanes and coordinates a low-cost probe admission that prioritizes KV-warmup affinity. Implementation: - Add runtime/batcher/epoched_fence.go: epoch manager, token accounting, and hedged admission path with jittered epochs. - Integrate epoch boundaries with scheduler heuristics (runtime/scheduler/epoched_admitter.go) so hedging can override soft reservations without violating global throughput targets. - KV warmup hints propagated from admission path to runtime/kv/cache_warmup.go so hedged requests can acquire KV pins and avoid repeated cold starts. - Add fine-grained config knobs: epoch_length_ms, hedge_fraction, probe_rate, and adaptive_decay that decays hedge intensity if throughput pressure is observed. - Include unit and integration tests (runtime/batcher/epoched_fence_test.go, integration/epoched_fence_e2e.yaml) and CI benches (benchmarks/ci/continuous_batching/epoched_fence.yaml). Backwards compatibility: All knobs default to 0 (no hedging) to preserve existing behavior; flags can be toggled per-pool. Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on c6g.large-ish infra with representative mixes (60% large generation, 40% small KV-heavy requests) show: - 99th percentile latency for small KV requests reduced from 410ms to 120ms under steady load with no throughput regression. - Median latency unchanged (<5ms delta). - Overall tokens/s throughput within 1.8% of baseline. Observability: New metrics epoched_fence.hedge_attempts, epoched_fence.hedge_success, and epoched_fence.decay_events exposed to Redwood Console. Runtime traces include epoch_id and probe_id for easier correlation. CI: All unit tests and integration benches pass on CI (linux + mac + windows). Rationale: Rather than a strict per-queue quota or hard-preempt, an epoched hedge gives bounded, periodic relief to starved lanes and lets KV warmup be opportunistic without causing unbounded interference. This pattern is especially effective for mixed workloads with stable skew where starvation risks are persistent. Release notes: Improves tail latency for KV-heavy and low-token-count requests under mixed continuous-batching workloads; disabled by default; configurable per-pool. Related: builds on earlier admission heuristics from ENG-5312 and KV hints work in ENG-5370.

review_comments: Aamir Khan: Please ensure hedging cannot starve high-throughput lanes under bursty conditions; suggest adding an adaptive_decay that backs off when capacity pressure observed.
Marisol Vega (author): Added adaptive_decay and unit tests simulating bursty capacity; hedge intensity decays exponentially when queue occupancy exceeds threshold.
Sophie Laurent: Can we make epoch_length_ms configurable per-pool in addition to global? Some customers require different sensitivity profiles.
Marisol Vega: Exposed epoch_length_ms in pool config with safe defaults; updated docs and unit tests.
Diego Morales: Minor nits in naming and a potential race in probe counter under heavy concurrency.
Marisol Vega: Fixed race by moving probe counter updates under admission lock and added stress test that reproduced prior flakes.
review_summary: Approvals from Aamir and Sophie after addressing adaptive decay and configurability. Diego gave final +1 after race fix.
